caseStudyHeader.heading: Predictive Customer Analytics (PCA)
caseStudyHeader.body: A cloud-based product for marketing analysts at a time when campaigns need to be personal and timely.

summary.title: Outcome
summary.description: I brought the product from its initial user and market need framing to its limited released to clients.

summary.title: Goal
summary.description: The product needed to simplify and integrate predictive analytics into the core workflows of marketing analysts.

summary.title: Role
summary.description: I was the primary product designer. My role was diverse and my most lasting contribution was defining the product's core user flow.

summary.title: Client and scope
summary.description: The internal client was the IBM Analytics product division and I spent one year working on the product between 2015 and 2016.

context.statement: How might we design a better way for marketing analysts to identify customers for a sales campaign?
list: IBM Analytics needed to combine its SPSS and Cognos capabilities to meet marketing's growing need for personalized, timely campaigns.
Marketing analysts relied on spreadsheet-based tools that performed poorly at scale, lacked engagement-system integration, and couldn't leverage predictive analytics without a data scientist.
Analysts were beholden to data scientists to build predictive models, limiting how targeted their campaigns could be.
The vision was to democratize predictive analytics — giving analysts a dynamic, integrated way to build and act on customer lists themselves.

images.alt: The home screen: a bubble chart of high attrition audiences with one list selected on the left, and a grid of recent customer lists on the right.
The Customer scorecard for a list: six rolling seven-day averages, including customers, attrition and CLTV, beside a line chart of customers over time.
The Attrition lens, "High risk customers by segment": a bubble chart of attrition score by customer lifetime value, with three written insights on the right.

subsections.subhead: Manually edit customer lists with rules

images.alt: The Edit view: a list of rules such as age, city and education on the left, and a bar chart of customers by age with the 30 to 50 range highlighted.
The Export view, "Select a destination", with four options: share via UBX, publish to IBM Marketing Cloud, save basic data to desktop, or save all data to desktop.

process.statement: The biggest challenge was convincing stakeholders to match the product’s workflow with user needs.
process.description: Stakeholders initially favored a conventional file-management model, while research revealed a cyclical analytical workflow. The resulting workspace connected customer lists with the analysis workflow, enabling analysts to move bidirectionally between understanding and shaping the lists.

list: PCA started as a market need with no defined user experience
I brought it from initial framing to a limited release with clients
I drove alignment across product, research and engineering to keep it moving
PCA merged into Watson Marketing Insights, later sold and spun out as Acoustic
